2026-W13:f737866ac3b5.editorialTake:
The real risk for luxury and jewellery brands is not AI replacing human touch, but missing how AI is quietly reshaping the rules of access, trust, and discovery. At the same time, TikTok Shop’s transaction volume surged 80 percent year over year, with over 103 billion e-commerce searches driving major brand sales. These moves are connected. As De Beers limits access, it is echoing a broader shift: who gets to play in the luxury supply chain is being redrawn by both old-guard gatekeepers and new digital platforms. TikTok Shop’s surge shows that discovery is no longer about who owns the best real estate, but who can surface the right product to the right customer at the right moment—something AI is now doing better than ever. Oracle’s AI-driven procurement tools mean that even behind the scenes, the rules of engagement are changing fast: brands can automate away weak links, spot risks, and enforce standards with a precision that was impossible a year ago.

Skeptics argue that luxury is immune to these shifts, that heritage and physical experience will always trump digital and data. But Home Depot’s record foot traffic, even as it leans into AI-powered omnichannel, shows that automation and physical relevance are not opposites. The brands that win will be those that use AI to reinforce, not replace, their core value: trust, scarcity, and storytelling.

For jewellery and luxury operators, now is the time to audit your supply chain partners, test AI-powered discovery on emerging platforms, and tighten control over distribution. The next quarter will reward those who treat AI not as a threat, but as a tool to redraw the boundaries of exclusivity and customer connection.

2026-W16:06b32c2dcdb4.editorialTake:

Will this force a new wave of consolidation or push rivals to double down on partnerships with telecom giants? Amazon’s bet on satellite infrastructure challenges the assumption that ecommerce growth depends solely on digital innovation rather than physical network control.

The strongest counterargument is that AI and hardware wars are still a step removed from daily retail, and that gold prices always fluctuate. But the pace and scale are different now. When OpenAI loses three senior executives at once, and Canva repositions itself as an AI platform, it is clear that the competitive ground is shifting fast.

For luxury and jewellery brands, the implication is clear: treat your tech stack and supply chain as strategic assets, not cost centers. Secure your access to AI tools and digital infrastructure now, before pricing power shifts further upstream. And with gold volatility set to continue, lock in margins with hedging or creative pricing. The winners will be those who can operate at both ends of the value chain—controlling the story, and the silicon it runs on.

2026-W18:570b4f42b95c.editorialTake:

2026-W19:519ce372a162.editorialTake:

The winners will be those who combine human expertise with the new machine backbone, not those who hope tradition alone will hold the line.

2026-W20:fe32458efb35.editorialTake:
